title: Cloud-Native Networking, CNI, eBPF & Ingress Routing
summary: Master Kubernetes Pod-to-Pod networking, Cilium eBPF dataplanes, CoreDNS service discovery, ClusterIP/LoadBalancer EndpointSlices, and Ingress / Gateway API routing.
learningObjectives: Understand the Kubernetes network model where every Pod receives a routable IP without NAT.
Diagnose and repair broken Services with 0 endpoints caused by label selector mismatches.
Configure L7 Ingress resources routing external HTTPS traffic to internal ClusterIP services.

curriculumModules.title: CNI Architecture, Cilium eBPF & EndpointSlices
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Container Network Interface (CNI) plugins allocate Pod IPs and program node routing. Modern eBPF CNIs like Cilium replace linear iptables chains with O(1) kernel socket-level hash maps.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Run Cilium in kube-proxy-less eBPF mode with EndpointSlices enabled to scale clusters beyond 5,000 services with sub-millisecond service routing.

curriculumModules.title: CoreDNS Service Discovery & Ingress / Gateway API
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: CoreDNS resolves `<service>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local` to ClusterIP VIPs, while Ingress and Gateway API controllers terminate TLS and route L7 HTTP/gRPC traffic.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Expose internal microservices as `ClusterIP` Services and route external north-south traffic through a redundant Ingress/Gateway controller protected by WAF.

labs.title: Repairing Zero-Endpoint Service Selector Drift
labs.scenario: Deployment `catalog-api` in `production` has 2 running pods labeled `app=catalog-api`, but Service `catalog-svc` has `0 endpoints` because its selector points to `app=catalog-v1-old`.
labs.productionContext: Service selector drift silently drops traffic (`503 Bad Gateway`) even when all backing pods report `1/1 Running`.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: catalog-svc
  namespace: production
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: catalog-api
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 80

steps.title: Inspect Service Endpoints
steps.instruction: Run `kubectl get svc catalog-svc -n production` to observe that ENDPOINTS is `<none>`.

validationRules.description: Service production/catalog-svc selector set to app=catalog-api
validationRules.name: catalog-svc
catalog-svc
validationRules.remediation: Ensure catalog-api pods are Running and matched by catalog-svc.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Check `kubectl get svc catalog-svc -n production` to verify ENDPOINTS lists two Pod IPs.

labs.title: Exposing Production Workloads via L7 Ingress Controller
labs.scenario: Expose the `storefront` deployment in `production` via a `ClusterIP` service and create an `Ingress` resource named `storefront-ingress`.
labs.productionContext: Production clusters avoid creating a cloud LoadBalancer per microservice; instead, a single Ingress/Gateway routes host/path traffic to internal ClusterIP services.
objectives: Expose deployment `storefront` as service `storefront` on port 80 in `production`
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: storefront-ingress
  namespace: production
spec:
  ingressClassName: cilium
  rules:
    - host: shop.kubelabs.io

steps.title: Expose Storefront Deployment as ClusterIP Service

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure both Service `storefront` and Ingress `storefront-ingress` exist in the `production` namespace.

assessmentQuestions.question: What happens when a Kubernetes Service exists in a namespace, but its `spec.selector` labels do not match any running Pods?
options: Kubernetes automatically relabels all pods in the namespace
The Service is created with a ClusterIP, but its EndpointSlice remains empty (`0 endpoints`), causing traffic to fail
kube-apiserver rejects the Service creation with HTTP 422
CoreDNS refuses to create an A record for the Service
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Services and Pods are loosely coupled via label selectors. If no running, ready pods match the selector, the Service has 0 endpoints.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does Cilium eBPF improve service load-balancing performance compared to legacy iptables kube-proxy?
options: By using O(1) eBPF kernel hash maps at the socket layer instead of traversing O(N) sequential iptables rules
By routing all traffic through a central NAT instance
By requiring static IP addresses for every container
assessmentQuestions.explanation: iptables rules grow linearly O(N) with service count, whereas Cilium eBPF performs O(1) hash table lookups directly at socket connect/sendmsg time.
